items.t: Big Bend is the City of Burnaby's main agricultural area in south Burnaby, on the Fraser River foreshore flats below the city's steep south slope — primarily an industrial and agricultural district, not a conventional residential neighbourhood. It combines ALR farmland, the Big Bend industrial lands along the river, Burnaby Fraser Foreshore Park, and a small rural-residential component (the Riverside area). "Big Bend" is the GVR board sub-area name in the SnapStats GVR September 2026 report under community "Burnaby," and it matches the name the City itself uses for its south Burnaby agricultural area.
Where the condo stock concentrates: nowhere — there is no verified apartment-condo concentration in this district.
There is no Big Bend sub-area median.

Main streets: Marine Way / Marine Drive runs along the top of the foreshore flats, and Byrne Road and Sussex Avenue descend to the river lands; Highway 1 and the Edmonds / Metrotown town centres are north up the slope.

Transit anchors: there is no SkyTrain station in Big Bend; the district is car- and truck-served, and specific TransLink bus routes serving the foreshore streets were not confirmed pass — not verified.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Big Bend

items.t: City zoning — current bylaw: Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815) was adopted June 9, 2026 and took effect July 1, 2026, replacing the former Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 1965 (Bylaw No. 4742), which is repealed and should be flagged as such wherever a source still cites it. For Big Bend specifically: A1 is the City's agricultural zoning district (chickens may be kept in the A1 district under Zoning Bylaw rules), and the City is updating zoning regulations for agricultural districts through the 2026 rewrite — parcel-level minimum lot sizes and the current district for a specific farm parcel: Not verified, confirm in writing with the City and the ALC.

ALR — the district's defining rule: ALR status and permitted farm / non-farm uses for a specific property are checked in the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR Property and Map Finder, and ALR land is governed by the provincial Agricultural Land Commission Act framework. The Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan, adopted December 9, 2025, supports protecting and expanding agriculture in Big Bend.

Flood — the second defining rule: the City states the nearly 800 hectares of low-lying land between the south slope and the Fraser River is a floodplain; the Fraser River poses a substantial flood hazard from snowmelt in late spring and early summer and from combined heavy rain and winter storm surge events. The City protects the lowland with river and shoreline dykes, pump stations and flood boxes, maintains a Flood Response Plan, and receives regular updates from the BC River Forecast Centre during flooding events and freshet. Confirm a parcel's flood construction requirements, dyke position and insurance before subjects come off.

blocks.text: Good to know about Big Bend

items.t: The "condo market" here is three listings and no sales. Any page copy implying a Big Bend condo scene would be inventing one.

The farming heritage is Chinese Canadian, and it is documented by the City. The City states Big Bend has a culturally diverse farming heritage, with historic Chinese Canadian small-scale farms that still exist today, and runs a Burnaby Farm Tour Map promoting farm-gate and nursery sales in the district.

The 2050 OCP points this district away from housing, not toward it. The Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan, adopted December 9, 2025, supports protecting and expanding agriculture in Big Bend — the opposite direction from the town-centre densification the same plan drives elsewhere in Burnaby.
The flood protection is a system, not a single dyke. Which reach a parcel sits behind is a per-parcel check.

The agricultural zoning was mid-rewrite when the new bylaw landed. The Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (adopted June 9, 2026, in effect July 1, 2026) replaced the 1965 bylaw city-wide, and the City is updating zoning regulations for agricultural districts through that rewrite — a Big Bend zoning letter written off the old bylaw can already be stale.

There is no in-area school, library or hospital to market. None was confirmed inside the district pass — services sit up the slope (Tommy Douglas Library, 7311 Kingsway; Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St). Copy claiming in-area amenities for a Big Bend property should be treated as unverified until a source states it.

The City describes the lowland as nearly 800 hectares between the steep south slope and the river, along nearly 7 km of the North Arm of the Fraser River. Nearby areas: South Slope and Garden Village above the bluff to the north, Edmonds to the north-east, the Glenlyon / Byrne Creek industrial lands within the wider south Burnaby employment area, and Richmond across the North Arm to the south. Marine Way / Marine Drive runs along the top of the foreshore flats and Byrne Road and Sussex Avenue descend to the river lands.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates: nowhere —. (SnapStats, September 2026)

Community context (SnapStats publishes medians at community level only — there is no Big Bend sub-area median): Burnaby condos & townhomes median was $686,000 in September 2026 ($763/sqft, 98% sale-to-list, 36 days on market), cited exactly as the report states it, as "Condos & Townhomes" COMBINED, never as a townhome-only figure — and in Big Bend's case it prices other sub-areas' stock, not anything in this district. (SnapStats, September 2026)

Flood — the district's second defining fact: the nearly 800 hectares of low-lying area between the steep south slope and the Fraser River is a floodplain; the Fraser River poses a substantial flood hazard from snowmelt in late spring and early summer and from combined heavy rain and winter storm surge events. The City protects the lowland with river and shoreline dykes, pump stations and flood boxes, maintains a Flood Response Plan, and receives regular updates from the BC River Forecast Centre during flooding events and freshet.

Agriculture — the defining fact: land in Big Bend is in the provincial Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR), administered by the Agricultural Land Commission, and the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan supports protecting and expanding agriculture in Big Bend. The City runs a Burnaby Farm Tour Map for the Big Bend farming district, promoting farm-gate and nursery sales, and states Big Bend has a culturally diverse farming heritage, with historic Chinese Canadian small-scale farms that still exist today. A1 is the City's agricultural zoning district in Big Bend (chickens may be kept in the A1 district under Zoning Bylaw rules).

Schools, library, health, transit: no public school inside Big Bend was confirmed on the Province's SD41 list — SD41 has no middle-school tier (elementary K–7, secondary 8–12), catchments are address-based, and the specific schools for a Big Bend / Riverside address are not verified (check the exact address in the SD41 locator). The nearest library branch is the Tommy Douglas Branch, 7311 Kingsway, up the slope in Edmonds; the city's hospital is Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St. There is no SkyTrain station in Big Bend — the district is car- and truck-served, and specific TransLink bus routes serving the foreshore streets were not confirmed: Not verified.

items.t: The rules that actually decide a Big Bend purchase come first, because there is no townhouse stock here: ALR and flood: ALR status and permitted farm / non-farm uses for a specific property are checked in the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR Property and Map Finder, and ALR land is governed by the provincial Agricultural Land Commission Act framework — run the ALR check before pricing development or non-farm value into any parcel. Flood: the district is a roughly 800-hectare Fraser River floodplain protected by dykes, pump stations and flood boxes — confirm the parcel's flood construction requirements, dyke position and insurance before subjects come off, not after.

Strata rules — stated because they would govern any strata lot a buyer did find in the district, and because an unnamed attached listing count exists: Form B diligence: Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. If a property marketed as "Big Bend" carries no strata plan, there is no Form B — verify the tenure before applying strata diligence at all.

blocks.text: Good to know about Big Bend

items.t: Zero is the honest market statistic. (SnapStats, September 2026)

The farming heritage is specific, and the City documents it. Big Bend has a culturally diverse farming heritage, with historic Chinese Canadian small-scale farms that still exist today, and the City promotes the district's farm-gate and nursery sales on its Burnaby Farm Tour Map — the agricultural offer here is working farms, not a rural aesthetic.

The employment-land figure uses a different map. Industrial space accounts for nearly half of Burnaby's employment space city-wide in the City's employment lands work, with the Big Bend sub-area accounting for much of it on the City's assessment geography — that geography is a City-study boundary, not the MLS sub-area boundary, so the figure cannot be quoted as an MLS Big Bend statistic.

Burnaby's zoning bylaw changed mid-2026, mid-farm-season. The Zoning Bylaw 2026, No. 14815, took effect July 1, 2026, replacing the 1965 bylaw (No. 4742), with agricultural-district regulations being updated through the rewrite — an A1 assumption taken from the old bylaw is not enough for a farm purchase closing after that date.

The flood system reports in. During flooding events and freshet the City receives regular updates from the BC River Forecast Centre and maintains a Flood Response Plan for the lowland — a Riverside or farm buyer can ask what the parcel's position is relative to the dykes, pump stations and flood boxes that make up that system.

There is no population to quote. A Big Bend–only population figure is not verified — no official source read states one, because the district is mostly farmland, park and industrial land. Any page giving Big Bend a neighbourhood population is inventing it.

items.t: Big Bend is in the City of Burnaby, BC — the City's main agricultural area in south Burnaby, on the Fraser River foreshore flats below the city's steep south slope. "Big Bend" is the GVR board sub-area name as it appears in the SnapStats GVR September 2026 report under community "Burnaby", and it matches the name the City of Burnaby itself uses for its south Burnaby agricultural area. (SnapStats, September 2026)

Nearby areas: South Slope and Garden Village above the bluff to the north, Edmonds to the north-east, the Glenlyon / Byrne Creek industrial lands within the wider south Burnaby employment area, and Richmond across the North Arm of the Fraser River to the south.

Roads and transit: Marine Way / Marine Drive runs along the top of the foreshore flats and Byrne Road and Sussex Avenue descend to the river lands; Highway 1 and the Edmonds / Metrotown town centres are north up the slope. Commute times in minutes: Not verified.

The nearest library branch is the Tommy Douglas Branch, 7311 Kingsway, up the slope in Edmonds (Burnaby Public Library has four branches, one in each quadrant). The city's hospital is Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St (Fraser Health), in central Burnaby. Farm-gate and nursery sales in the Big Bend farming district are promoted on the City's Burnaby Farm Tour Map; a main shopping centre in the area is not confirmed on an official source: Not verified — everyday shopping is up the slope in Edmonds and South Slope.

Schools: public schools are run by School District 41 (Burnaby), which operates 41 elementary and 8 secondary schools city-wide; SD41 has no middle-school tier (elementary K–7, secondary 8–12). No completed locator run is documented for this ground. School names are Ministry-listed names, spelled exactly.

Market context, labelled correctly: Burnaby IS a SnapStats-covered community, and SnapStats has NO land category — the figures here are labelled community/sub-area context only, never land figures. Burnaby community detached median $1,825,000 and condos & townhomes median $686,000. Sub-area medians are not verified (SnapStats publishes medians at community level only).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Big Bend

items.t: Zoning — Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026, No. 14815 (in effect July 1, 2026): the new Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 was adopted June 9, 2026 and took effect July 1, 2026, and the City is updating zoning regulations for agricultural districts through that rewrite. A1 is the City's agricultural zoning district in Big Bend (chickens may be kept in the A1 district under Zoning Bylaw rules). Parcel-level minimum lot sizes and the current district for a specific Big Bend farm parcel: Not verified — an A1 assumption from the old bylaw is not enough for a farm purchase; verify the current zoning district in writing with the City and the ALC.

Subdivision + servicing — process documented, base number HELD not confirmed: subdivision of a Big Bend parcel runs through the City's subdivision process under its subdivision servicing bylaw framework, with servicing standards confirmed with the City for the specific parcel and, for ALR parcels, ALC approval engaged first (below).

ALR block — the governing rules for Big Bend farm ground: subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR. ALR status and permitted farm / non-farm uses for a specific property are checked in the ALC's ALR Property and Map Finder, and ALR land is governed by the provincial Agricultural Land Commission Act framework — run the ALR check first on any farm parcel, before pricing development or non-farm value into it.

Floodplain diligence — the second defining fact: the City states Burnaby's southern boundary borders nearly 7 km of the North Arm of the Fraser River and the nearly 800 hectares of low-lying area between the steep south slope and the Fraser River is a floodplain; the Fraser River poses a substantial flood hazard from snowmelt in late spring and early summer and from combined heavy rain and winter storm surge events. The City protects the lowland areas with river and shoreline dykes, pump stations and flood boxes, maintains a Flood Response Plan, and receives regular updates from the BC River Forecast Centre during flooding events and freshet. Confirm the parcel's flood construction requirements, dyke position and insurance before subjects come off, not after.

Burnaby property taxes and farm class: City of Burnaby property taxes for 2026 were due Friday, July 3, 2026; a 5% penalty applies to outstanding current taxes after the July due date, with a further 5% penalty after the September due date. Farm-class assessment and tax treatment for a specific Big Bend parcel is a BC Assessment / tax-notice check per property: Not verified here — confirm farm-class status and what transfers with the sale, because the tax treatment drives the carrying cost. Burnaby's published 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, sewer use and garbage fees for residential properties; farm and industrial utility charges for a specific Big Bend property: Not verified.
